timeline.title: Election Schedule Announcement
timeline.description: The Election Commission of India (ECI) officially announces the 7-phase schedule for the 2024 Lok Sabha elections.

timeline.title: Model Code of Conduct Enforced
timeline.description: Immediately following the schedule announcement, the MCC comes into effect across the entire country.

timeline.title: Phase 1 Polling Begins
timeline.description: The first and largest phase of voting commences, covering 102 constituencies across 21 states and union territories.

timeline.title: Final Phase (Phase 7) Polling
timeline.description: The final phase of voting concludes the democratic exercise for the remaining 57 constituencies.

timeline.title: Counting & Results Declaration
timeline.description: Official vote counting by the ECI across all centers, leading to the final declaration of the 18th Lok Sabha results.

quiz.question: What is the minimum voting age for citizens in India?
quiz.explanation: According to the 61st Amendment Act of 1988, the voting age in India was lowered from 21 to 18 years.

quiz.question: What does EVM stand for in the Indian election system?
quiz.explanation: EVMs are Electronic Voting Machines used by the Election Commission of India to record votes securely.

quiz.question: Which document is primarily issued by the ECI as proof of identity for voting?
quiz.explanation: EPIC (Electors Photo Identity Card), commonly known as Voter ID, is issued by the ECI specifically for voting.

quiz.question: Who appoints the Chief Election Commissioner of India?
quiz.explanation: The President of India appoints the Chief Election Commissioner and other Election Commissioners.

quiz.question: What does VVPAT stand for?
quiz.explanation: VVPAT provides a paper slip to voters confirming their vote was cast correctly.

quiz.question: What is NOT allowed during the Model Code of Conduct period?
quiz.explanation: Once MCC is in effect, the ruling party cannot announce new financial grants or projects to influence voters.

quiz.question: NOTA is an option on the EVM. What does it stand for?
quiz.explanation: NOTA allows voters to officially register their rejection of all candidates in the election.

quiz.question: What is the maximum number of candidates an EVM can cater to (including NOTA) using a single Ballot Unit?
quiz.explanation: A single Ballot Unit can accommodate 16 candidates including NOTA. Up to 24 units can be connected together.

quiz.question: Which article of the Indian Constitution establishes the Election Commission of India?
quiz.explanation: Article 324 vests the superintendence, direction, and control of elections in the Election Commission.

quiz.question: When is National Voters' Day celebrated in India?
quiz.explanation: National Voters' Day is celebrated on January 25 every year to mark the foundation day of the Election Commission of India.

quiz.question: Which body conducts elections to the Panchayats and Municipalities?
quiz.explanation: While the ECI handles national and state assembly elections, local body elections are handled by State Election Commissions.

quiz.question: What is the security deposit amount for a Lok Sabha candidate from the general category?
quiz.explanation: A candidate contesting a Lok Sabha election must deposit Rs. 25,000 (Rs. 12,500 for SC/ST).

quiz.question: How many hours before polling must election campaigning officially end?
quiz.explanation: Campaigning must stop 48 hours before the conclusion of polling to give voters a peaceful period to think.

quiz.question: Which of these is used to mark a voter's finger to prevent double voting?
quiz.explanation: Indelible ink, containing silver nitrate, is applied to the left index finger and cannot be easily washed off.

quiz.question: What is the maximum limit on election expenditure for a Lok Sabha constituency (as of recent revisions)?
quiz.explanation: For bigger states, the expenditure limit for a Lok Sabha candidate is Rs. 95 Lakhs.

quiz.question: Who was the first Chief Election Commissioner of independent India?
quiz.explanation: Sukumar Sen served as the first Chief Election Commissioner of India from 1950 to 1958.

quiz.question: Can an NRI (Non-Resident Indian) vote in Indian elections?
options: Yes, in person at their registered constituency
quiz.answer: Yes, in person at their registered constituency
quiz.explanation: NRIs who hold Indian citizenship can vote, but currently, they must be physically present at their polling station.

quiz.question: What is the role of a Returning Officer (RO)?
options: Conducts the election in a constituency
quiz.answer: Conducts the election in a constituency
quiz.explanation: The RO is the statutory authority responsible for the conduct of elections in a specific constituency.

quiz.question: Which form is used for the inclusion of names in the electoral roll for first-time voters?
quiz.explanation: Form 6 is used to apply for inclusion of your name in the voter list if you are a new voter.

quiz.question: When does the term of a newly elected Lok Sabha officially begin?
quiz.explanation: The term of the Lok Sabha is five years from the date appointed for its first meeting.

quiz.question: Who is the Constitutional Head of the Executive in India?
quiz.explanation: The President is the constitutional head of the executive of the Union.

quiz.question: What is the maximum strength of the Lok Sabha allowed by the Constitution?
quiz.explanation: The maximum strength of the House is 550 members (after removing the Anglo-Indian reserved seats).

quiz.question: Which of these is NOT a national party in India currently?
quiz.explanation: Shiv Sena is a State recognized party, not a National Party.

quiz.question: What is the minimum age to become a Member of Parliament in the Lok Sabha?
quiz.explanation: Article 84 of the Constitution mandates a minimum age of 25 years for the Lok Sabha.

quiz.question: Who administers the oath of office to the President of India?
quiz.explanation: The Chief Justice of India administers the oath to the President.

quiz.question: Which body resolves disputes relating to the election of the President?
quiz.explanation: All doubts and disputes regarding the election of a President or Vice-President are inquired into and decided by the Supreme Court.

quiz.question: What does Delimitation mean in the context of Indian elections?
quiz.explanation: Delimitation is the act of redrawing the boundaries of an assembly or Lok Sabha seat to represent changes in population.

quiz.question: EVMs were first used in which state's assembly election?
quiz.explanation: EVMs were first used in the Parur Assembly Constituency of Kerala in 1982.

quiz.question: Which color of ballot paper is typically used for Lok Sabha elections when EVMs are not used?
quiz.explanation: White ballot papers are generally used for Lok Sabha elections, while pink is for Assembly elections.

quiz.question: What is the tenure of the Chief Election Commissioner?
options: 6 years or up to 65 years of age
quiz.answer: 6 years or up to 65 years of age
quiz.explanation: The CEC has a tenure of 6 years or up to the age of 65, whichever is earlier.

quiz.question: Who reserves the election symbols for political parties?
quiz.explanation: The ECI is responsible for the allotment of symbols to political parties and candidates.

quiz.question: What is an Exit Poll?
options: A post-voting survey of voters leaving polling booths
quiz.answer: A post-voting survey of voters leaving polling booths
quiz.explanation: Exit polls are surveys conducted immediately after voters leave the polling stations to predict the result.

quiz.question: Which constitutional amendment made the right to form cooperative societies a fundamental right?
quiz.explanation: The 97th Amendment Act of 2011 gave constitutional status and protection to cooperative societies.

quiz.question: Can a person confined in prison vote in Indian elections?
options: No, prisoners lose their voting rights
Yes, if permitted by the jailer
quiz.answer: No, prisoners lose their voting rights
quiz.explanation: Under Section 62(5) of the Representation of the People Act, 1951, individuals confined in a prison cannot vote.

quiz.question: What is the role of a Presiding Officer?
options: To manage the polling station on election day
quiz.answer: To manage the polling station on election day
quiz.explanation: The Presiding Officer is in charge of a polling booth and ensures the poll is conducted smoothly and fairly.

quiz.question: Who can vote using a Postal Ballot?
options: Armed forces personnel and specific officials on duty
quiz.answer: Armed forces personnel and specific officials on duty
quiz.explanation: Postal ballots are restricted to specific groups like armed forces, officials on election duty, and preventive detainees.

quiz.question: What is the maximum age to vote in India?
options: There is no maximum age limit
quiz.answer: There is no maximum age limit
quiz.explanation: There is no upper age limit for voting in India. Any citizen 18 or older can vote.

quiz.question: Who designed the Indian EVM?
quiz.explanation: EVMs were designed and developed by Bharat Electronics Limited (BEL) and Electronics Corporation of India Limited (ECIL).

quiz.question: What happens if a candidate's votes are less than 1/6th of the total valid votes polled?
options: They are banned from next election
quiz.explanation: If a candidate fails to secure at least one-sixth of the valid votes polled, their security deposit is forfeited.

quiz.question: What does a 'Star Campaigner' mean?
options: A designated prominent campaigner for a recognized party whose expenses are not added to the candidate's limit
quiz.answer: A designated prominent campaigner for a recognized party whose expenses are not added to the candidate's limit
quiz.explanation: Recognized political parties can have up to 40 Star Campaigners whose travel expenses are borne by the party, not the individual candidate.

quiz.question: What is the minimum number of electors required to propose a candidate for Lok Sabha?
quiz.explanation: For a candidate set up by a recognized National/State party, only 1 elector from the constituency is needed as a proposer.

quiz.question: Which App allows citizens to report Model Code of Conduct violations?
quiz.explanation: The cVIGIL app empowers citizens to report MCC and expenditure violations during elections.

quiz.question: What is the quorum required to hold a meeting of the Lok Sabha?
quiz.explanation: The quorum to constitute a meeting of either House of Parliament is one-tenth of the total number of members.

quiz.question: What is the 'None of the Above' (NOTA) button colored?
options: It does not have a specific color, but is the last panel
quiz.answer: It does not have a specific color, but is the last panel
quiz.explanation: NOTA is placed as the last option on the ballot unit and doesn't have a distinct standardized color requirement.

quiz.question: How long is the term of a Rajya Sabha member?
quiz.explanation: Members of the Rajya Sabha are elected for a term of six years, with one-third retiring every second year.

quiz.question: Who decides the date of elections in India?
quiz.explanation: The ECI has the sole constitutional authority to announce election schedules.

quiz.question: What is an Electoral Bond?
options: A financial instrument for making anonymous donations to political parties
A bond signed by a candidate
quiz.answer: A financial instrument for making anonymous donations to political parties
quiz.explanation: Electoral bonds were bearer instruments used to donate funds to political parties (recently struck down by the SC).

quiz.question: Who is eligible to register as an overseas elector?
options: An NRI holding an Indian passport who has not acquired citizenship of any other country
quiz.answer: An NRI holding an Indian passport who has not acquired citizenship of any other country
quiz.explanation: Only NRIs who are citizens of India and have not acquired foreign citizenship can register as overseas voters.

quiz.question: What is the maximum time gap allowed between two sessions of Parliament?
quiz.explanation: The Constitution mandates that there should not be a gap of more than six months between two sessions of Parliament.

quiz.question: Which of these is considered a 'Corrupt Practice' under election law?
options: Appealing for votes on the grounds of religion
quiz.answer: Appealing for votes on the grounds of religion
quiz.explanation: Appealing to voters in the name of religion, race, caste, or community is a corrupt practice under the RPA, 1951.

history.description: The first general election of independent India. It took five months to complete due to the sheer size and challenging geography of the country.
The second general election. The INC retained power with a massive majority, winning 371 seats.
The third general election saw Jawaharlal Nehru elected for a third consecutive term, though his party lost some seats compared to previous elections.
The first election after the deaths of Nehru and Lal Bahadur Shastri. Indira Gandhi led the INC to victory, but with a significantly reduced majority.
Held after a split in the Congress party. Indira Gandhi's faction, campaigning on the slogan 'Garibi Hatao' (Remove Poverty), won a landslide victory.
A historic election following the Emergency (1975-1977). The INC lost power for the first time at the center, leading to the first non-Congress government.
Following the collapse of the Janata Party government due to internal conflicts, Indira Gandhi returned to power with a strong majority.
Held immediately after the assassination of Indira Gandhi. The INC won 404 seats, the highest number ever won by any party in Indian history.
Resulted in a hung parliament. The Janata Dal formed the National Front government with outside support from the BJP and Left parties.
Marred by the assassination of Rajiv Gandhi mid-campaign. The INC emerged as the largest party and formed a minority government.
Resulted in a fractured mandate. The BJP formed a 13-day government, followed by the United Front coalition supported by the INC.
The BJP-led NDA formed a government that lasted 13 months before losing a confidence motion by exactly one vote.
Held after the Kargil War. The NDA secured a clear majority, and Atal Bihari Vajpayee became the first non-Congress PM to complete a full 5-year term.
A surprising defeat for the NDA's 'India Shining' campaign. The Congress-led UPA formed the government with support from Left parties.
The UPA returned to power with an increased mandate. Manmohan Singh became the first PM since Nehru to be re-elected after completing a full five-year term.
The BJP achieved an absolute majority on its own (282 seats), marking the first time since 1984 a single party won a majority without coalition support.
The BJP secured an even larger majority, winning 303 seats. It was the highest ever voter turnout recorded in Indian history at the time.
The BJP-led NDA secured a third consecutive term, though relying more on alliance partners as the BJP did not cross the absolute majority mark alone.
